claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'GENERATE statement, XIII-66' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'GENERATE statement, XIII-66' then '  Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300dpi render of page 967 (printed B-55) against page-967.md. The markdown source holds every entry on its own line with sub-entries indented two spaces beneath their main entry (e.g. 'GENERATE statement, XIII-66' / '  Imperative statement, IV-39'; 'GIVING phrase' / '  ADD statement, VI-73' ...), which mirrors the printed one-entry-per-line, indented-sub-entry layout. The claim itself concedes the entry text and page references match. The only difference is markup style (bare lines vs. '- ' list items used on pp. 961-962) and how a Markdown renderer would reflow it: a formatting/rendering concern with no change to the transcribed content or the hierarchy as encoded in the source text. Formatting-only differences are rejected.
